comment: IDENTITY PROFILE for the owner-data ship gate. These are the strings that identify THE PERSON BUILDING THIS PRODUCT, and none of them may reach a stranger's disk. They live here, not in tools/check-no-owner-data.mjs, because identity is user data: a second person building this product has a different name, username, account aliases and LAN range, and would otherwise have to edit a tool to be protected. The MECHANISM (walk the bundle, match bytes, fail closed) is in code; these VALUES are settings. See config/owner-data-patterns.example.json to start your own.
matching: Entries are matched as raw bytes anywhere in any shipped file, case-insensitively by default. Set caseSensitive: true where case carries meaning (an IP range, a case-sensitive identifier).
ownership: This file is committed so the owner's configuration survives a fresh clone -- and is therefore INHERITED by anyone who clones the repository. To stop a stranger's build from passing a guard aimed at the wrong person, the gate requires at least one pattern here to relate to the OS account running the build (case-insensitive substring, either direction; "joshp" below is what matches this fleet). A different builder replaces these values with their own; a build machine whose account name legitimately differs sets MC_IDENTITY_PROFILE_ACCOUNT to the account this profile describes.

patterns.note: Windows username; appears in every home-directory path.
Private LAN range for this fleet. Case-sensitive: it is digits, and a case-folded match would be meaningless.
Owner's real name as prose. Found shipping inside app.asar after four path-shaped patterns all passed clean.
Surname alone, for the cases where the given name is absent.
University account. Found shipping in src/vocab.js and src/views/metrics.js as simulation pool names. No name-shaped or path-shaped pattern caught it: an alias is neither.
Second account alias, same class as above.
